To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the EF results for products can differ considerably depending on the inclusion of nutrients and non-C2O greenhouse gases.
the EF results of specific products are sensitive to the inclusion of non-CO2 emissions and nutrient emissions.

the ecological footprint of waste treatment processes is dominated by nutrient emissions, the EF of bio-based energy is mainly determined by non-CO2 gases and the EF of agricultural products and chemicals is mainly determined by land use.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of nutrients and other greenhouse gases on EF calculations and shows the importance of including these stressors in EF studies.
the relevance of including non-CO2 gases and nutrient emissions in the EF assessment.

the question of whether or not the EF is a useful tool for the analysis of product-related environmental impacts and whether or not the method should be improved to better represent the ecological reality.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the EF methodology is not suitable for the assessment of the impact of nutrients and non-C02 greenhouse gases on a product level.
the EF is a valuable tool to assess the environmental impacts of products, but that it should be used with care and with a clear focus on the environmental stressor(s) that are of interest.
the EF should not be extended to other stressors, but that it should rather be applied as a tool to analyze the relative importance of different stressors for specific product categories.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
nutrients and non-C2O greenhouse gases are relevant to include in the EF assessment for products with high nutrient and non-CO greenhouse gas emissions.
the EF is not a perfect indicator for sustainability, but that the indicator is still a useful instrument to assess and communicate sustainability.
the EF is an appropriate indicator to assess land use for human activities and the EF results can be significantly influenced by including nutrient and non-CO 2 greenhouse gas emissions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the EF should be used as an indicator for the overall environmental impact of products and services.
the EF should be extended with nutrients and greenhouse gases to better assess the environmental impacts of human activities.
the EF is not a static concept and that the EF methodology needs to be updated to account for new environmental challenges.
